title: Diagnose tenant upgrade lockfile corruption and deploy surgical hotpatch
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Several customers running Private/VPC deployments observed tenant upgrades failing with a corrupted lockfile on the operator side which left tenants in a partial-apply state. Symptoms: helm upgrade returns success, operator reconcile fails to complete, CRs record a manifest checksum mismatch and API surface shows stale status. Impact: customer workloads degraded (API 503s) while operator repeatedly attempted idempotent applies and held a stale lock, blocking progress and preventing automatic rollback. This ticket captures diagnosis, short-term surgical hotpatch, and rollout plan for safe remediation.
steps_to_reproduce: Start operator v2.14.0 on a cluster with multi-tenant onprem config
Simulate concurrent helm upgrade + operator reconcile by triggering a bulk tenant manifest change across 12 tenants
Observe helm upgrade logs (helm v3) indicate successful release but operator logs show repeated 'apply partial' errors and 'lockfile checksum mismatch'
Query tenant CR status and watch for 'manifest_shadow' and 'reconcile_in_progress' conditions
Check node filesystem for /var/lib/redwood/operator/locks/<tenant> lockfile with truncated JSON/EOF
Verify client-facing errors (503s) for affected tenant routes and increased operator.apply.partial_count metric
timeline: 2026-03-10: Customer support escalated via SE — multiple tenants reporting stuck upgrades and 5xx errors
2026-03-10: On-call Eng team reproduced a partial-apply locally with race between helm post-render and operator CR update
2026-03-11: Added telemetry metric operator.apply.partial_count and a debug logging flag to capture lockfile writes (PR #14567)
2026-03-12: Identified root cause — non-atomic lockfile replace during concurrent reconcile + helm release hooks caused truncated/partial JSON leading to corrupted lock state
2026-03-13: Drafted surgical hotpatch to make lockfile writes atomic and add a checksum/fast-validate before acquiring lock (branch hotfix/lockfile-atomic)
2026-03-14: Canary rollout to 3 low-risk tenants in staging cluster succeeded — operator resumed and cleared stuck reconciles. Monitoring OK. Rolling to customer staging tenants next.
2026-03-15: Plan to coordinate customer remediation windows and full rollout to production clusters if canary is green for 48h
mitigation: Applied a configuration-level mitigation for affected tenants: disabled parallel upgrade worker pool (operator.workers=1) per-tenant to stop concurrent writes and kicked reconciles in a controlled window. Notified customers and scheduled per-tenant resyncs. This is a temporary measure to reduce blast radius while hotpatch is validated.
proposed_fix: Hotpatch implements atomic lockfile write (write-to-temp-then-rename), embed a 64-bit CRC in the header, and validate checksum before acquiring a lock. Add a fast repair path: if checksum invalid, operator will attempt a read-merge from k8s API + helm release and produce an advisory event instead of blocking. Also add e2e test and chaos test that simulates concurrent helm/operator operations.
acceptance_criteria: Canary rollout (3 tenants) shows no recurrence for 48h
operator.apply.partial_count returns to baseline and never spikes during staged upgrades
Automated e2e that simulates concurrent helm and operator reconcile passes in CI
Documentation updated: runbook for manual healing and per-tenant resync steps
Customer escalations closed with postmortem and remediation notes
notes: Trade-off: chose minimally invasive atomic write + checksum instead of full operator rearchitecture to meet customer deadlines
Longer-term follow-up: evaluate replacing filesystem locks with leader-election-based distributed locks (ENG-Q3 project) and reconcile idempotency hardening

Risk: rename-based atomic write assumes underlying filesystem semantics on customer nodes — we validated on commonly used distro images in staging but will include platform compatibility checks in preflight
Coordination: SEs to propose maintenance windows for high-risk customers; Solutions Eng will run remediation playbook for enterprise tenants
Post-deploy: schedule a short blameless postmortem and add synthetic test covering parallel upgrade scenario to weekly regression suite
